sourceEvidence.label: RAG TM-05/TM-07 threat-model and source evidence

assessment.summary: Two owned-boundary changes can remove the remaining filesystem check/open race and destructive Qdrant synchronization window.

nonNegotiables: Preserve existing public RAG HTTP contracts
Keep file and journal I/O bounded
Preserve current tactical protections during migration
assumptions: No measured latency, memory, or Qdrant storage budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Own ingest containment at the file-open boundary
opportunities.summary: Add a Kujo descriptor-relative no-follow read and migrate RAG ingest callers.
opportunities.diagnosis: RAG containment checks and Kujo file opening are separate operations over a mutable pathname.

evidence.claim: TM-05 records repeated path checks and a remaining check/open race.
Kujo bounds generic reads but does not expose a descriptor-relative no-follow read.
A mutable component can be substituted between caller validation and generic path opening.

desiredInvariants: The root and every traversed component are pinned by handles before the final object is read.
Symlink, reparse, absolute, parent, special-file, and oversized targets fail closed.
Unsupported platforms never fall back to check-then-open semantics.

options.title: Repeated local guards
options.summary: Retain generic reads and repeat containment checks immediately before opening.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Additional checks narrow timing but do not bind them to the open.
The generic runtime boundary remains unchanged.

tradeoffs.assessment: More checks reject more static substitutions, but the race remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run rename and symlink stress against every ingest read.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each added metadata check adds filesystem calls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark shallow and deep ingest paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded path and metadata values are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS on a large file inventory.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure behavior stays familiar, while races remain nondeterministic.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Repeat concurrent replacement tests and classify errors.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new component is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm existing path rejection telemetry is sufficient.

tradeoffs.assessment: No public API changes are needed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run current ingest compatibility coverage.

workPackages: Repeat pre-open checks and retain regression coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: Static traversal and symlink inputs are rejected.

options.title: Descriptor-relative capability read
options.summary: Move containment and opening into one Kujo-owned operation.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The owned operation removes the pathname check/open race after caller migration.
Kujo gains the missing safe boundary as an additive API.

tradeoffs.assessment: Handle-relative no-follow traversal binds proof to effect.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise component substitution and reparse/symlink PoCs on every supported OS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Traversal opens each component, adding system calls off the query path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark 1-, 5-, and 20-component paths at representative file sizes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Handles and read buffers remain bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record peak handles and RSS during maximum-depth reads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unsafe substitutions become deterministic errors.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run concurrent rename stress and descriptor-leak tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: New rejection and unsupported-platform codes require telemetry.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify logs and alerts distinguish policy rejection from I/O failure.

tradeoffs.assessment: Kujo platform work and caller migration are required, though the API is additive.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Canary one parser and run full compatibility suites.

residualRisks: In-place mutation of an already-open regular file is outside the contract.

acceptanceCriteria: No untrusted component is pathname-resolved after containment proof.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Switch RAG back to tactical guards while retaining the additive API.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the Kujo-owned capability API and retain local checks during migration.

opportunities.title: Make Qdrant synchronization a recoverable commit
opportunities.summary: Stage a generation, verify it, atomically switch an alias, then reconcile the local mirror.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current remote collection is deleted before the replacement is verified and before local persistence commits.

evidence.claim: Synchronization deletes the active collection before create and upsert, and local persistence follows remote sync.
Failure coverage verifies the local mirror is preserved but does not model remote preservation.
A crash or remote failure can leave the queryable remote state empty or divergent despite a false save result.

desiredInvariants: The active remote generation remains readable until a complete candidate is verified.
One atomic alias operation selects the visible generation.
A durable bounded journal makes every phase idempotently recoverable.
Successful saves prove matching local and remote generation metadata.

options.title: Destructive replacement with stronger alerts
options.summary: Persist retry state and alert on divergence while retaining delete-first replacement.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Retries improve recovery but active state is still deleted first.
Coverage can assert alerts and retry state, not atomicity.
Operational recovery improves while transaction residual remains.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durable retry reduces silent divergence but does not protect active data.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failures after delete, create, and upsert.

tradeoffs.assessment: Candidate persistence adds one bounded local write.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure ingest time and disk bytes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Retry state can remain on disk and bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS during maximum index retry.

tradeoffs.assessment: Restart can retry, but remote availability still has a destructive window.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Crash after each phase and measure recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Alerts and retry ownership are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise alert and runbook paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Collection naming and query behavior stay compatible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing backend and privacy tests.

residualRisks: Active remote collection can be absent or incomplete until retry succeeds.

acceptanceCriteria: Failed sync produces durable retry state and an actionable alert.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable retry worker and retain the candidate for manual recovery.

options.title: Staged generation and atomic alias commit
options.summary: Verify an isolated generation before atomically making it visible.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The active collection is no longer destructively replaced before verification.
New remote-state and recovery assertions close the current test gap.
The protocol defines a commit point and restart recovery for strict Qdrant mode.

tradeoffs.assessment: Candidate failure cannot destroy the active generation before commit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject every state edge and verify the active alias target.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ingest adds verification; steady query alias routing should be neutral.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark ingest and query latency against a pinned live Qdrant.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local buffers remain bounded, while remote temporary storage increases.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS and staged-generation storage.

tradeoffs.assessment: A durable state machine supports idempotent recovery and alias rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restart after every phase and repeat recovery twice.

tradeoffs.assessment: Generation inventory, journals, GC, and alias telemetry are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run operator recovery and GC drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing collections require alias bootstrap and new configuration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse bootstrap and rollback on a production-shaped staging copy.

residualRisks: Qdrant control-plane compromise and operator deletion remain outside the application transaction.

acceptanceCriteria: No pre-commit failure changes the active alias target.
Successful commits match local and remote metadata.
migrationNotes: Bootstrap an alias to the existing collection and retain legacy mode outside strict configuration for one release.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Atomically switch the alias to the prior retained generation and reconcile the local mirror.

opportunities.recommendation: Require staged alias commits in strict mode after a compatibility release and live-Qdrant validation.

openQuestions: Which Windows handle-relative primitive and minimum version will Kujo support?
Which Qdrant versions and alias operations form the supported contract?
How is vector dimension supplied for a first empty generation?
What retention and storage ceilings govern old-generation garbage collection?
